_readme: CPE-1950. The shared oracle for the CPE-1903 auto-merged-platform-config guard, which exists
verify-release-artifacts, i.e. release.yml's tag path) and the mirror in
Both implementations run every case below, so a change to one that the other does not follow reds
on the side that made it. Same shape as shellScriptLines.cases.json.
If you touch EITHER implementation, add the case HERE, never to one side's own test.
WHAT THIS CANNOT CATCH: shared blindness. A shared oracle proves the two agree; it cannot prove
either is right. A filename shape or a merge-patch shape that neither implementation considered
is simply absent from this file, both sides answer it the same wrong way, and this passes. That
is not hypothetical -- on PR #1060 a `<<` inside a quoted string opened a phantom heredoc in BOTH
the TS and Rust shell scanners and the shared case file agreed with itself. The independent legs
are what cover it: the TS suite derives TAURI_PLATFORM_TOKENS from the Rust const at run time
(so a token added on one side reds without anyone writing a case), and each side keeps its own
tests for the properties the other cannot express.

names.name: the base config is NOT auto-merged (other guards pin it by value)
the base config in json5 is not auto-merged either
the base TOML config is not auto-merged
an explicit --config overlay is CONFIG_CHAIN's business, not this guard's
a per-platform --config overlay: second segment is `sidecar`, not a platform token
a format tail Tauri has not shipped yet still matches (shape, not enumeration)
the >= 3 segment rule: a bare `tauri.windows` has no format tail, Tauri never reads it
a trailing dot DOES give a third (empty) segment -- both sides must agree which way this falls
a non-ASCII letter in the `tauri` segment matches on neither side (both folds leave it)

refusals.name: strict JSON setting plugins.updater
RFC 7396 null DELETES the updater block -- refused just as hard as a replacement
CPE-1903 finding 9: a null `plugins` deletes the parent, and so the child
finding 9: a non-object `plugins` replaces the whole block
finding 9: a string `plugins`
finding 9: a number `plugins`
a non-object ROOT replaces the entire config
an array root
a string root
a number root
a per-platform file that does not touch the updater stays ALLOWED
...and one that only sets bundle targets
TOML this guard cannot parse but can still clear

TOML table header naming the updater
TOML dotted key naming the updater
escaped so the literal token never appears -- the backslash arm catches it
unparseable, no updater token, no backslash: allowed

empty file: strict-JSON parse fails, no token, no backslash -- allowed
